name: theme-replay-stage0-memo-comparison
question_answered: Does model disagreement improve an evidence-linked analytic memo?
memo_writer_note: A model stands in for the human analyst. It is outside the three analysis families so it does not favour its own reading. It is a proxy, not the human H or H+M arm.

conditions.S: corpus plus one reading: family f, run 1. One memo per family.
conditions.R: corpus plus three readings from the SAME family f (runs 1..3) plus the divergence view. One memo per family. Same volume and format as M; the readings differ only by repeat drift.
conditions.M: corpus plus three readings, one per family, all from run k, plus the divergence view. One memo per k in 1..3.

primary_contrast: M versus R. Both give three readings and a divergence view. Only M varies the model family.
presentation: Readings are labelled A, B, C in a seeded shuffle. No model id reaches the writer. Each reading carries its verify errors.
hard_failures: a memo citation whose quote does not resolve on the cited line
a claimed_status that differs from the status on the cited line
an episode id that does not exist
output that is not the JSON object

engagement_proxies.note: Citation-pattern proxies computed from the corpus structure, fixed before any output. They show that a memo engages a feature of the corpus with grounded evidence. They do not show that the memo's sentence about it is right.
engagement_proxies.F1: one claim cites correction lines from at least 2 of E04, E08, E12
engagement_proxies.F2: one claim cites, in the same episode, a correction line and an event:succeeded line
engagement_proxies.F3: the memo cites at least 2 event:unknown lines with claimed_status unknown
engagement_proxies.F4: one claim cites event:failed lines from at least 2 of E02, E06, E10
engagement_proxies.F5: one claim cites both E02 and E04

decision_rule.YES: M mean proxy count exceeds R mean by at least 1.0, M has zero hard failures, and M mean (exception + open_question claims) is at least R mean.
decision_rule.NO: M mean proxy count is at or below both R mean and S mean, or M has more hard failures than R.
decision_rule.limits: n = 3 memos per condition on 12 synthetic episodes. A YES here shows mechanics can carry a difference. It is not evidence that the method helps on real work. Oscar's blind rating of the memo packet is the gate for that.
